---
title: "1_Find_Peaks_By_Specificity"
output: html_document
date: "2025-10-07"
---

This script finds regional peaks based on specificity scoring (the 
kind-of-fraction of that peak's reads found in the Region_NT). Will find
shared GABA/Glut peaks by balancing the highest specificity between the two
Region_NTs.

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
    library(dplyr)
    library(ComplexHeatmap)
    library(circlize)
    library(RColorBrewer)
    library(ggplot2)
    library(patchwork)
})


theme_md_classic <- function() {
    theme_classic(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        plot.title  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        axis.title  = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.text   = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks  = element_line(color = "black"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text  = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}
```


```{r}
repo <- here::here()  # root of this repository (run from anywhere inside it)
pdir <- file.path(repo, "3_Analysis/ATAC_Regional_Analysis")
path_mat <- file.path(pdir, "common_data/Cluster_v4_by_462k_peaks_matrix.csv")
path_obs <- file.path(pdir, "common_data/Cluster_v4_by_462k_peaks_obs.csv")
outdir   <- file.path(pdir, "RegionalPeaksBySpecificity")

pdir_plots <- file.path(outdir, "plots")
if (!dir.exists(pdir_plots))
    dir.create(pdir_plots)
```

# Normalize matrix

```{r}
mat_norm <- edgeR::cpm(mat)
```

Z-scoring the whole matrix is expensive, so will only do as needed.

# Heatmap code (cands_by_region)

the essence:


```{r}
make_heatmap <- function(cands_by_region, regions = useable_regions, Z_CLIP=6) {
    
    ## ---------------- config ----------------
    region_levels <- regions                         # enforce this order for rows & cols
    region_pal    <- setNames(brewer.pal(length(region_levels), "Set2"), region_levels)
    
    # preferred NT ordering (others appended afterward)
    nt_preferred  <- c("Glut", "GABA")
    
    # heatmap colors
    hm_cols <- colorRamp2(c(-Z_CLIP, 0, Z_CLIP), c("#38598C", "white", "#B40426"))
    
    ## -------- rows (peaks) from top20 lists, grouped by region ----------
    peaks_concat <- unlist(cands_by_region[region_levels], use.names = FALSE)
    peaks_concat <- peaks_concat[!is.na(peaks_concat)]
    
    peak_region_vec <- unlist(
        lapply(region_levels, function(rg) rep(rg, length(cands_by_region[[rg]]))),
        use.names = FALSE
    )
    peak_region_vec <- peak_region_vec[seq_along(peaks_concat)]
    peak_region_fac <- factor(peak_region_vec, levels = region_levels)
    
    ## ------- columns (clusters), grouped by region, THEN ordered by NT ------
    # keep only clusters in the chosen regions
    obs_sub <- obs %>%
        filter(Dominant_Region %in% region_levels)
    
    # NT levels: preferred first (if present), then all remaining NTs
    nt_all     <- as.character(obs_sub$NT)
    nt_levels  <- c(nt_preferred[nt_preferred %in% nt_all],
                    setdiff(sort(unique(nt_all)), nt_preferred))
    
    # palette for NTs (works for any # of categories)
    nt_pal <- setNames(colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"))(length(nt_levels)), nt_levels)
    
    # enforce factor levels and order columns by Region -> NT -> original order
    obs_sub <- obs_sub %>%
        mutate(
            Dominant_Region = factor(as.character(Dominant_Region), levels = region_levels),
            NT = factor(as.character(NT), levels = nt_levels)
        )
    col_order <- rownames(arrange(obs_sub, Dominant_Region, NT))
    col_region_fac <- factor(as.character(obs_sub[col_order, "Dominant_Region", drop = TRUE]),
                             levels = region_levels)
    col_nt_fac     <- factor(as.character(obs_sub[col_order, "NT", drop = TRUE]),
                             levels = nt_levels)
    
    ## -------- matrix subset + z-score per peak (row) ----------
    peaks_present <- intersect(peaks_concat, rownames(mat_norm))
    if (length(peaks_present) == 0) 
        stop("No selected peaks found in matrix.")
    
    keep_idx <- peaks_concat %in% peaks_present
    peaks_concat    <- peaks_concat[keep_idx]
    peak_region_fac <- droplevels(peak_region_fac[keep_idx])
    
    mat_sub <- mat_norm[peaks_concat, col_order, drop = FALSE]
    mat_z <- t(scale(t(mat_sub)))
    mat_z[is.na(mat_z)] <- 0
    mat_z[mat_z >  Z_CLIP] <-  Z_CLIP
    mat_z[mat_z < -Z_CLIP] <- -Z_CLIP
    
    ## -------------- annotations ---------------
    row_anno <- rowAnnotation(
        PeakRegion = peak_region_fac,
        col = list(PeakRegion = region_pal),
        show_annotation_name = TRUE,
        annotation_name_side = "top",
        annotation_legend_param = list(title = "Peak region")
    )
    
    top_anno <- HeatmapAnnotation(
        ClusterRegion = col_region_fac,
        NT            = col_nt_fac,
        col = list(
            ClusterRegion = region_pal,
            NT            = nt_pal
        ),
        show_annotation_name = TRUE,
        annotation_name_side = "left",
        annotation_height = unit(c(3, 3), "mm")  # tweak bar heights if needed
    )
    
    ## -------------- heatmap -------------------
    ht <- Heatmap(
        mat_z,
        name = "z",
        col = hm_cols,
        cluster_rows = FALSE,
        cluster_columns = FALSE,
        show_row_names = FALSE,
        show_column_names = FALSE,
        row_split = peak_region_fac,      # row slice order follows region_levels
        column_split = col_region_fac,    # column slice order follows region_levels
        top_annotation = top_anno,
        left_annotation = row_anno,
        row_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
        column_gap = unit(2, "mm"),
        border = TRUE,
        column_title = "clusters grouped by dominant region & neurotransmitter",
        row_title = "candidate peaks grouped by region"
    )
    return(ht)
}
```


# Ensure sharing across NTs

## Peak specificity by region+NT

Copy most of code above, but do the specificity by region+NT:

```{r}
peak_sums <- rowSums(mat_norm)
```

```{r}
regions_nt <- unlist(lapply(useable_regions, paste0, "_", c("GABA", "Glut")))
```

```{r}
peak_sums_regions_nt <- lapply(regions_nt, function(rg_nt) {
    rg <- sub("_.*", "", rg_nt)
    nt <- sub(".*_", "", rg_nt)
    idx <- which(
        (obs$Dominant_Region == rg) & (obs$NT == nt)
    )
    rowSums(mat_norm[, idx])
})
names(peak_sums_regions_nt) <- regions_nt
```

```{r}
frac_in_region_nt <- lapply(peak_sums_regions_nt, "/", peak_sums)
```

## Peak specificity by region only (use only GABA/Glut)

Used later on.

```{r}
peak_sums_regions <- lapply(useable_regions, function(rg) {
    idx <- which(
        (obs$Dominant_Region == rg) & (obs$NT %in% c("GABA", "Glut"))
    )
    rowSums(mat_norm[, idx])
})
names(peak_sums_regions) <- useable_regions
```

```{r}
frac_in_region <- lapply(peak_sums_regions, "/", peak_sums)
```

## Plot region+NT expression vs. specificity


Although, I have to say, the units are so impossible to comprehend. Each cluster
is normalized to have a million reads, and there are 1810 clusters. If
every peak were even, each peak would have 2.16 normalized reads in each cluster,
which would sum to 3911 reads across all clusters (log10=3.6). But each region
only has a minority of clusters, so the sum is kind of hard to interpret. 
Instead, a better unit would be to average the clusters, so at least there's 
some kind of normalization between the regions (and some interpretability).

In this case, the "average" peak would be 2.16 normalized reads in each cluster,
or 0.33 on the x-axis.

**Note:** this and basically the same plots are repeated below, but they can 
make even good peaks look bad if they're only in subsets of the selected 
clusters. However, those peaks will also look bad in the genome browser because
of the heterogeneity in the grouping variable.


```{r}
for (rg_nt in regions_nt) {
    rg <- sub("_.*", "", rg_nt)
    nt <- sub(".*_", "", rg_nt)
    idx <- which(
        (obs$Dominant_Region == rg) & (obs$NT == nt)
    )
    plot(log10(peak_sums_regions_nt[[rg_nt]] / length(idx)), frac_in_region_nt[[rg_nt]], 
         main=rg_nt, 
         xlab="log10[avg cpm in region+NT clusters]", 
         ylab="fraction of peak's reads in region+NT")
}
```

*To improve*: Need to show everything, the exp/specificity in each NT side-by-side,
but maybe color points by the combined ranks (or highlight the top ones), and
maybe also a rank-rank plot side-by-side with those...
[done below, after getting combined ranks]

MB Glut is really weak.

Otherwise, real signal seems to be important for having a high rank, so I think
the ranks are useable as-is.

Get ranks of each peak in each region+nt [higher is more expressed]:

## Candidates via combined ranks

### Get combined ranks (Glut&GABA)

```{r}
ranks_frac_by_region_nt <- lapply(frac_in_region_nt, rank)
```

```{r}
# for later, not used right here
ranks_frac_by_region <- lapply(frac_in_region, rank)
```


For each region and peak, get the combined ranks of the Glut+GABA:

```{r}
comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region <- lapply(useable_regions, function(rg) {
    nm_glut <- paste0(rg, "_Glut")
    nm_gaba <- paste0(rg, "_GABA")
    out <- ranks_frac_by_region_nt[[nm_glut]] + ranks_frac_by_region_nt[[nm_gaba]]
    names(out) <- names(ranks_frac_by_region_nt[[nm_glut]]) # =rownames(mat)
    out
})
names(comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region) <- useable_regions
```

Later on, I end up using the reverse ranks for stuff, not sure if I should do
that for everything.

### Plot specificity vs. expression & combined ranks

3 plots side-by-side: exp-vs-specificity for each NT, and then also plot 
specificities against. In all 3, color by combined rank (or maybe just the top20).

```{r}
dir_plt <- file.path(pdir_plots, "plots_diagnostic_combined_spec_ranks")
if (!dir.exists(dir_plt))
    dir.create(dir_plt)
```


```{r, fig.width=16, fig.height=6}
# will show the avg cpm in a cluster for if all peaks were uniformly distributed
exp_for_unif <- log10(1e6 / nrow(mat))

# total peaks (for recalculating ranks)
n_peaks <- nrow(mat)

for (rg in useable_regions) {
    rg_gl <- paste0(rg, "_Glut")
    rg_ga <- paste0(rg, "_GABA")
    ncl_gl <- length(which((obs$Dominant_Region == rg) & (obs$NT == "Glut")))
    ncl_ga <- length(which((obs$Dominant_Region == rg) & (obs$NT == "GABA")))
    
    # for these plots, invert rank so it's easy to highlight the top ones using
    # log scaling (naturally highlights the lowest numbers, smears together the
    # highest). Because combined ranks have weird numbers (variable ranges),
    # will calculate the rank of the combined-ranks, and then invert those
    # ranks
    
    df_gl <- data.frame(
        avg_exp    = log10(peak_sums_regions_nt[[rg_gl]] / ncl_gl),
        frac_reads = frac_in_region_nt[[rg_gl]],
        comb_rank  = n_peaks - rank(comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region[[rg]])
    ) %>% 
        .[order(.$comb_rank, decreasing = TRUE), ]
    df_ga <- data.frame(
        avg_exp    = log10(peak_sums_regions_nt[[rg_ga]] / ncl_ga),
        frac_reads = frac_in_region_nt[[rg_ga]],
        comb_rank  = n_peaks - rank(comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region[[rg]])
    ) %>% 
        .[order(.$comb_rank, decreasing = TRUE), ]
    
    df_ss <- data.frame(
        frac_gl = frac_in_region_nt[[rg_gl]],
        frac_ga = frac_in_region_nt[[rg_ga]],
        comb_rank = n_peaks - rank(comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region[[rg]])
    ) %>% 
        .[order(.$comb_rank, decreasing = TRUE), ]
    
    p1 <- ggplot(df_gl, aes(avg_exp, frac_reads, color = comb_rank)) +
        geom_point() +
        geom_vline(xintercept = exp_for_unif, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = "dashed") +
        scale_color_viridis_c(trans="log10", direction=-1) + 
        labs(
            title = rg_gl, 
            x = paste0("avg cpm in ", rg_gl, " clusters (log10)"),
            y = paste0("peak specificity\n(fraction normalized reads in ", rg_gl, ")"),
            color = "combined specificity\nranks, in reverse-rank\norder"
        ) + 
        theme_md_classic()
    
    p2 <- ggplot(df_ga, aes(avg_exp, frac_reads, color = comb_rank)) +
        geom_point() +
        geom_vline(xintercept = exp_for_unif, linewidth = 0.25, linetype = "dashed") +
        scale_color_viridis_c(trans="log10", direction=-1) + 
        labs(
            title = rg_ga, 
            x = paste0("avg cpm in ", rg_ga, " clusters (log10)"),
            y = paste0("peak specificity\n(fraction normalized reads in ", rg_ga, ")"),
            color = "combined specificity\nranks, in reverse-rank\norder"
        ) + 
        theme_md_classic()
    
    p3 <- ggplot(df_ss, aes(frac_gl, frac_ga, color = comb_rank)) + 
        geom_point() + 
        geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linewidth = 0.25) +
        scale_color_viridis_c(trans="log10", direction=-1) + 
        labs(
            title = rg,
            x = "peak specificity Glut", 
            y = "peak specificity GABA", 
            color = "combined specificity\nranks, in reverse-rank\norder"
        ) + 
        theme_md_classic()
    
    ggsave(
        file.path(dir_plt, paste0(rg, ".png")),
        p1 + p2 + p3 + plot_layout(guides = "collect"),
        width = 16, height = 6
    )
}
```

I think what I've done is better than if I had added together the actual 
specificity scores because those could be blown out by really specific peaks in
one NT, whereas this flattens that quantitative issue.

### Heatmap top20 by combined rank

For each region, get the top20 peaks by combined rank (in Glut & GABA):

```{r}
top20_peaks_by_comb_rank_region <- lapply(comb_ranks_of_nt_by_region, function(x) {
    ord <- order(x)
    idx <- tail(ord, 20)
    rownames(mat_norm)[idx]
})
```

```{r, fig.width=20, fig.height=20}
ht <- make_heatmap(top20_peaks_by_comb_rank_region)
draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right", annotation_legend_side = "right")
```

```{r}
pdf(
    file.path(pdir_plots, "heatmap_top20_by_combined_rank.pdf"),
    width=20, height=16
)
draw(ht, heatmap_legend_side = "right", annotation_legend_side = "right")
invisible(dev.off())
```

You know, I think this logic should work? But maybe funny things can happen
when the NTs aren't balanced, the ranks might not combine in the best way for
truly shared peaks.

But there's also an issue when you look for the peaks with highest regional
enrichment due to the imbalance.

Overall it looks like I am finding shared peaks, but it's not always clear to 
me that the specificity is high for the region.

The confusion between THM_GABA and MB_GABA is weird looking. It's basically that
THM_GABA clusters have some of the MB peaks. But the MB signal is maybe weakest
so maybe not surprising...

Below, I found that there are like 50% more clusters in AMY now.

# Segregate regional clusters by candidate peak signal

In most/all cases, I can find a number of peaks shared between Glut & GABA, but
usually it's only a (consistent) subset of clusters within each NT that have
the peaks, and the other ones don't (often in both NTs).

It would be *tremendous* to discover, for instance, that the clusters that lack
those peaks are maybe less localized, so I want to aim to identify the clusters
that have the peaks vs. those that don't, and check their spatial mappings
visually.

I have the idea that kmeans w/ k=2 will basically sort the high-vs-low signal
clusters within each Dominant_Region.

```{r}
divide_clusters_by_candidates <- function(rg, cands_by_region) {
    # uses obs, mat_norm from global env
    cl <- rownames(obs)[which(obs$Dominant_Region == rg)]
    pk <- cands_by_region[[rg]]
    
    # zscore across all clusters before subset to clusters in region
    zmat <- t(scale(t(mat_norm[pk, ])))[, cl] 
    
    # divide clusters into 2 groups (hopefully "haves" and "have nots")
    cl_km <- kmeans(t(zmat), 2)
    
    # find the high-signal cluster [equal voting, not weighted by signal]
    cl_km_hi <- ifelse(
        (sum(cl_km$centers[1,] > cl_km$centers[2,]) / length(pk)) > 0.5,
        1, 2
    )
    
    hi_cl <- names(cl_km$cluster)[cl_km$cluster == cl_km_hi]
    lo_cl <- names(cl_km$cluster)[cl_km$cluster != cl_km_hi]
    
    list(
        cl       = cl,       # region cluster names
        pk       = pk,       # candidate peak names
        zmat     = zmat,     # zscored signal matrix (candidate peaks by region clusters)
        cl_km    = cl_km,    # kmeans cluster object
        cl_km_hi = cl_km_hi, # index of the kmeans cluster (1 or 2) that is high signal
        hi_cl    = hi_cl,    # clusters in the high signal kmeans group
        lo_cl    = lo_cl     # "             "  low signal "          "
    )
}
```

```{r}
grouped_clusts_by_candidates <- lapply(
    useable_regions, 
    divide_clusters_by_candidates, 
    top40_peaks_by_comb_rank_region
)
names(grouped_clusts_by_candidates) <- useable_regions
```

First, check if the kmeans groups are generally "low/hi" groupings:
(low being little candidate peak accessibility overall):

```{r}
# check if they are generally "low/hi" clusters
sapply(grouped_clusts_by_candidates, function(x) {
    h <- x$cl_km_hi
    l <- ifelse(h==1, 2, 1)
    sum(x$cl_km$centers[h, ] > x$cl_km$centers[l, ]) / length(x$pk)
})
```

## (!) Export regional clusters high-vs-low groups

```{r}
if (!dir.exists(file.path(outdir, "data")))
    dir.create(file.path(outdir, "data"))

dir_sv <- file.path(outdir, "data/regional_clusts_by_candidate_signal")
if (!dir.exists(dir_sv))
    dir.create(dir_sv)

for (rg in names(grouped_clusts_by_candidates)) {
    write(
        grouped_clusts_by_candidates[[rg]][["hi_cl"]],
        file.path(dir_sv, paste0(rg, "_High.txt"))
    )
    write(
        grouped_clusts_by_candidates[[rg]][["lo_cl"]],
        file.path(dir_sv, paste0(rg, "_Low.txt"))
    )
}
```

```{r}
lapply(grouped_clusts_by_candidates, function(x) {
    data.frame(
        sig_group  = rep(c("high", "low"), c(length(x$hi_cl), length(x$lo_cl))),
        cluster    = c(x$hi_cl, x$lo_cl)
    ) %>% 
        mutate(
            Subcortex_Group_v4 = obs[cluster, "Subcortex_Group_v4"]
        ) %>% 
        .[, c("sig_group", "Subcortex_Group_v4")] %>% 
        table %>% 
        t %>% 
        .[order(.[,"high"], decreasing = TRUE), ]
})
```

THM clusters.

# Find a score for across-NT regionality 

want a “regional, NT-shared specificity” score per peak that:
- rewards being highly specific to the region overall,
- balanced across Glut & GABA within that region (i.e., present in both),
- penalizes off-region signal, and
- (ideally) favors broad coverage across many clusters in that region (not just a few).

## (!) Precompute region/nt index sets

```{r}
# index of columns for each Region_NT
idx_by_rgnt <- lapply(useable_regions, function(rg) {
    list(
        Glut = which(obs$Dominant_Region == rg & obs$NT == "Glut"),
        GABA = which(obs$Dominant_Region == rg & obs$NT == "GABA")
    )
})
names(idx_by_rgnt) <- useable_regions

# index of columns for each Region (all NTs pooled)
idx_by_region <- lapply(useable_regions, function(rg) {
    which(obs$Dominant_Region == rg & obs$NT %in% c("Glut","GABA"))
})
names(idx_by_region) <- useable_regions

# all columns from usable regions (to define "off-region")
cols_in_scope <- sort(unique(unlist(idx_by_region)))
```

```{r}
# actually, relevant i think...
rgnt_pk_spec <- bind_rows(lapply(names(frac_in_region_nt), function(nm) {
    data.frame(
        peak = names(frac_in_region_nt[[nm]]),
        region_nt = nm,
        spec = frac_in_region_nt[[nm]],
        rank_spec = ranks_frac_by_region_nt[[nm]],
        row.names = NULL
    )
}))
rgnt_pk_spec <- mutate(
    rgnt_pk_spec, 
    rev_rank_spec = max(rank_spec) + 1 - rank_spec,
    region = sub("_.*", "", region_nt),
    nt     = sub(".*_", "", region_nt)
)
```

```{r}
rg_pk_spec <- bind_rows(lapply(names(frac_in_region), function(nm) {
    data.frame(
        peak = names(frac_in_region[[nm]]),
        region = nm,
        spec = frac_in_region[[nm]],
        rank_spec = ranks_frac_by_region[[nm]],
        row.names = NULL
    )
}))
rg_pk_spec <- mutate(rg_pk_spec, rev_rank_spec = max(rank_spec) + 1 - rank_spec)
```

```{r}
regionality_metric <- subset(rg_pk_spec, rev_rank_spec == 1000) %>% 
    arrange(desc(spec)) %>% 
    select(region, spec) %>% 
    rename(regionality = spec)
```
